activities.title: Grammar: Reporting the News (Passive Voice)
activities.instruction: News reports often use the passive voice to emphasize the action, not who did it. Rewrite the active sentences below into the passive voice.

sentences.original: The Romans built a giant dam nearly 2,000 years ago.
sentences.explanation: The object 'a giant dam' becomes the subject. We use 'was built' (past simple passive) because the action happened in the past.
sentences.transformed: A giant dam was built by the Romans nearly 2,000 years ago.

sentences.original: The authorities will demolish the old castle.
sentences.explanation: The object 'the old castle' becomes the subject. We use 'will be demolished' (future simple passive). We can omit 'by the authorities' as it's obvious.
sentences.transformed: The old castle will be demolished.

sentences.original: A rescue team rescued two swimmers from the sea.
sentences.explanation: The object 'two swimmers' becomes the subject. We use 'were rescued' (past simple passive).
sentences.transformed: Two swimmers were rescued from the sea.

sentences.original: Bird-watchers have seen a black stork in this country.
sentences.explanation: The object 'a black stork' becomes the subject. We use 'has been seen' (present perfect passive) because the original sentence is in the present perfect.
sentences.transformed: A black stork has been seen in this country.

Interviewer: And what happened exactly? Ed Shaw: In the hospital? Interviewer: Er, no. What happened when you collapsed? Mrs Shaw: I told him to wear a hat. Just that morning I'd said; Honey, don't forget your hat. It's gonna be hot today; And what did he say? 'It never gets hot in England. This isn't California; And what happens? He falls ... Ed Shaw: Honey, can you let me explain? We went for a walk in the hills - those hills over there - and it was fine. Ok, the sun was shining, but there was a slight breeze - a very pleasant gentle wind - and it didn't feel hot. Mrs Shaw: But then we stopped at a restaurant and where did he want to sit? Outside! content.transcript:
Don: I had a dream last night. Well, a nightmare, actually.
Jim: Really? What about?
Don: It was awful. I was terrified. There were men with horrible faces and...
Jim: Just a minute. Calm down. Begin at the beginning. Now ... Where were you?
Don: I dreamt that we were working in the fields and ...
Jim: Who was? Who were you with?
Don: My brother. My elder brother. We were planting seed for next year. And I was driving the tractor. And it was brilliant weather. Then suddenly ...
Jim: Slow down. Slow down. What happened?

sentences.text: Over the years there ___ (to be) many disastrous volcanic eruptions.
sentences.explanation: We use the Present Perfect ('have been') because 'Over the years' indicates a period of time that continues up to the present.

sentences.text: The worst ___ (to take place) in Krakatoa in 1883.
sentences.explanation: We use the Past Simple ('took place') because a specific past time ('in 1883') is mentioned.

sentences.text: Over 36,000 people ___ (to lose) their lives.
sentences.explanation: This event is part of the 1883 eruption, so we use the Past Simple ('lost').

sentences.text: A large passenger plane ___ (to crash) in the mountains.
sentences.explanation: We use the Present Perfect ('has crashed') to describe a recent event with a present result (the plane is still crashed, rescue is ongoing).

sentences.text: So far rescue teams ___ (to find) no survivors.
sentences.explanation: The phrase 'So far' indicates a period up to the present, so we use the Present Perfect ('have found').

sentences.text: The plane ___ (to take off) from London two days ago.
sentences.explanation: We use the Past Simple ('took off') because a specific past time ('two days ago') is mentioned.

sentences.text: The pilot ___ (to contact) Jeddah airport one hour before the plane crashed.
sentences.explanation: This action happened at a specific time before another past event, so we use the Past Simple ('contacted').

sentences.text: Several people ___ (to die) recently as a result of traffic accidents.
sentences.explanation: 'Recently' often signals the use of the Present Perfect ('have died') for recent past events with present relevance.

sentences.text: Last Thursday two small children ___ (to be) killed by a speeding car.
sentences.explanation: We use the Past Simple ('were') because a specific past time ('Last Thursday') is mentioned.

activities.title: Reporting the News
activities.instruction: Change the direct quotes from the news reports into reported (indirect) speech. Pay attention to changes in tense and pronouns.
activities.compensates: A traditional grammar exercise on reported speech, which is essential for writing a news report.

sentences.original: 'We urgently need tents and blankets,' a spokesman said.
sentences.explanation: In reported speech, 'we' changes to 'they' and the present tense 'need' changes to the past tense 'needed'.
sentences.transformed: A spokesman said that they urgently needed tents and blankets.

sentences.original: 'The buildings were very badly built,' said an eye-witness.
sentences.explanation: The past simple 'were' changes to the past perfect 'had been' in reported speech.
sentences.transformed: An eye-witness said that the buildings had been very badly built.

sentences.original: 'There is no clean drinking water,' said a nurse.
sentences.explanation: The present tense 'is' changes to the past tense 'was' in reported speech.
sentences.transformed: A nurse said that there was no clean drinking water.

sentences.original: 'Disease can spread very quickly,' she added.
sentences.explanation: The modal verb 'can' changes to 'could' in reported speech.
sentences.transformed: She added that disease could spread very quickly.
